name: Rudolf Hess
role: Deputy Führer of the Nazi Party (1933–1941); Reichsminister without portfolio (1933–1941)
summary: Rudolf Hess was Hitler's Deputy Führer and a close confidant until 1941. He argued for a single leader with unrestricted power against parliamentary majorities, backed the Nazi party's rule, the 1935 Nuremberg Laws and the annexations of Austria, the Sudetenland and Poland, and called for the destruction of Marxist and Bolshevik organizations. In May 1941 he flew to Scotland carrying peace terms, and he was later convicted at Nuremberg on the counts of crimes against peace and conspiracy.

sources.title: The Oath to Adolf Hitler (speech, 25 February 1934)
sources.author: Rudolf Hess
sources.usedFor: Broadcast oath speech: loyalty and absolute obedience to Hitler, leaders as examples, Hitler sent by higher powers, reason versus heart, service to the whole, Hitler Youth discipline

sources.title: Electing Adolf Hitler Führer (speech, August 1934)
sources.author: Rudolf Hess
sources.usedFor: Pre-referendum speech: argument for one leader with unrestricted power against parliament and separation of powers, providence, Roman dictatorship, plebiscite, Hitler's rise and the 1934 yes-vote appeal

sources.title: The Launching of the Training Ship Horst Wessel (speech, 1935)
sources.author: Rudolf Hess
sources.usedFor: Speech on naming a training ship: Horst Wessel as martyr, instilling loyalty to the Führer and to Germany in young men

sources.title: To the Front Fighters of the World (speech, 8 July 1934)
sources.author: Rudolf Hess
sources.usedFor: Speech on peace and armaments: front-soldier camaraderie, peace with France and Poland, limited German armaments, trade and peace, rejection of parliamentary majorities as representing interest groups

sources.title: From Revolution to Construction (speech, Gau Essen rally, 25 June 1934)
sources.author: Rudolf Hess
sources.usedFor: Speech on party unity: one movement instead of thirty parties, action against critics and saboteurs, Marxist organizations destroyed, Bolshevism and the 1934 'second revolution' dismissed, revolution directed by Hitler, rearmament of the economy and family and racial policy

sources.title: Reich Citizenship Law and Law for the Protection of German Blood and German Honor (15 September 1935)
sources.author: Reichstag (laws promulgated at Nuremberg; text as translated by USHMM)
sources.usedFor: Text of the two Nuremberg Laws, which bear Hess's signature as Deputy of the Führer on the Blood Law

sources.title: Judgment: Hess (Nuremberg International Military Tribunal)
sources.author: International Military Tribunal, Nuremberg
sources.usedFor: Tribunal's findings on Hess: supported rearmament and the 1935 conscription law, role in the Austria, Sudetenland and Poland annexations and decrees, the 1941 flight, and that proposed anti-Jewish laws were not sufficiently linked to war crimes

sources.title: Trial of the Major War Criminals, session of 31 August 1946 (Hess's final statement)
sources.author: Rudolf Hess
sources.usedFor: Hess's final statement at Nuremberg: refusal to defend himself against accusers, the Führer as his lifetime leader, no regrets, foreign-policy aims and armament, the 1923 revolution and atrocities, and his own religious belief

sources.title: Nuremberg trial transcript, prosecution case against Hess (7 February 1946)
sources.author: International Military Tribunal, Nuremberg (Harvard Law School Nuremberg Trials Project)
sources.usedFor: Prosecution quotations of a 28 August 1938 Hess speech to the Foreign Organization (Volksdeutsche, Sudeten Germans, Poland) and of the British record of Hess's May 1941 interview with the Duke of Hamilton, which gives his peace terms

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: He said a defenceless nation is a danger to peace and signed the conscription law.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: He defended the November 1923 putsch as a necessary act of resolve that showed the movement would act when needed.

arms-reduction.rationale: The IMT judgment records that he supported rearmament and signed the 1935 conscription law.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: He said parliamentary majorities represent interest groups and that parties before 1933 had sown hatred against the movement, which supports bypassing parties.

class-collaboration.rationale: He said class and rank collapsed at the front and that the movement brings Germans together across classes, rejecting class division.

class-struggle-history.rationale: He said Marxist organisations were destroyed and the nation is no longer divided by class.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: He urged sympathy for Germans in Czechoslovakia and supported Sudeten German claims, which rested on German nationality.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: In his 1941 peace terms he asked for the return of Germany's former colonies as a source of raw materials.

conscription.rationale: He signed the 16 March 1935 law restoring conscription.

consent-of-governed.rationale: He cited the 1934 plebiscite as public approval, while holding that the Führer's authority rests on providence and independence from earthly powers; the two points pull in different directions.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: He signed discriminatory laws and spoke of rejecting foreign blood.

decide-locally.rationale: He said central power overcame provincial resistance, and signed laws incorporating territories into central government.

defeat-communism.rationale: He said that saving Germany from Bolshevism rescued Europe from the danger of red annihilation.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: He remained loyal to Hitler to the end and said in 1946 he would act the same again.

democracy-best.rationale: He called parliamentary majorities irresponsible and unrepresentative of the people and argued that the Führer, not elected majorities, should hold power.

direct-action.rationale: He condemned revolt from below and agitation by revolutionary means, saying only Hitler directs the revolution, though he defended the 1923 armed attempt.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: He signed the Blood Law banning marriage between Jews and citizens of German blood, and the tribunal found his office proposed discriminatory laws.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: He said Hitler was sent to Germany by higher powers and that the Führer's authority reflects providence rather than a popular mandate.

duties-before-rights.rationale: He told party members to be ever servants of the whole and to think of the whole people before themselves, with duties above personal interest.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: He signed laws stripping Jews of citizenship and of marriage rights and spoke of racial cleanliness.

ethnic-nation.rationale: He wrote of preserving the family for racial cleanliness and rejecting foreign blood and spirit, to make the German people a racial community.

free-trade.rationale: He argued that unemployment is primarily the result of too little trade between nations and that trade is hindered by a lack of confidence.

independent-unions.rationale: He said the destruction of the organizations workers once belonged to was a prerequisite for economic recovery.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: At his Nuremberg trial he denied the right of his accusers to bring charges against him and rejected the charter of the tribunal as a historical falsehood.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: He spoke of the ideal of a greater Germany and supported the union of Austria with the German Reich.

leader-cult.rationale: He called Hitler the embodiment of a leader, the Führer, and said Adolf Hitler is Germany and Germany is Adolf Hitler, in a 1934 speech to a million party members.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: He honoured Horst Wessel and the fallen as heroes and martyrs of the movement and said a people without heroes will cease producing them.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: He said the movement was overcoming purely materialistic thinking and that spirit, not economic conditions alone, was the source of renewal.

member-state-blocks-federal-overreach.rationale: He praised the central power that overcame provincial resistance.

military-superiority.rationale: The IMT judgment records that he signed the 1935 conscription law and supported rearmament ('guns instead of butter').

minority-conspiracy.rationale: He spoke of Jewish rule in Hungary and an alleged Jewish aim in the League of Nations; the secondhand report of his views is contested, so this stays low.

moral-incentives.rationale: He praised sacrifice and the socialist deed as motives beyond pay.

multipolar-world.rationale: The prosecution's case records his 1941 peace terms dividing the world into an Axis sphere (Europe) and a British sphere (its empire).

nation-first.rationale: He said every great power pursued its own interests on a continental scale, and he defended German interests in those terms.

national-rebirth.rationale: He said the movement restores the German people's essence, pride and honor and frees it from international poisons and corruption.

natural-rulers.rationale: He held that the Führer, sent by higher powers, is Germany and rules by his own conscience, not by a mandate.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: He demanded absolute obedience that does not question orders or their reasons, obedience for its own sake.

one-party-rule.rationale: He said there was no single party in the old sense governing Germany, that the National Socialist movement gives direction to all political events, and that the parties before 1933 had fought the NSDAP.

parliament-supreme.rationale: He rejected parliamentary majorities as the basis of government and said the leader's action should not be watered down by parliamentary bodies.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: He demanded strict discipline and obedience to the Führer's orders from party officials and Hitler Youth leaders.

patriotic-education.rationale: He told the young sailors of a training ship to be imbued with loyalty to the Führer and with the spirit of service to the German nation.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: He said the German working class should be proud to back a national leader who came from it, tying loyalty to nation and the interests of workers.

person-over-state.rationale: He held that the individual owes the community sacrifice and obedience.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: He led the 1934 oath of loyalty and obedience sworn personally to Adolf Hitler by party leaders and Hitler Youth leaders.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: He spoke of the people returning to its essence and sources of strength and freeing itself from international poisons, which favors preserving national identity.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: The judgment records that he took the Sudeten German Party into the NSDAP and signed the Sudetenland decree of 14 April 1939.

race-social-construct.rationale: He treated race as a biological matter to be kept clean.

racial-franchise.rationale: He signed the 1935 regulation under which Jews could not be Reich citizens, vote or hold office.

racial-pride.rationale: He spoke of the pride of the German people and of Nordic mankind, which is pride in ancestry, though not a statement on pride in race as such.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The Nuremberg Laws classified people by blood and banned some marriages, but did not segregate housing, schooling or public facilities as the statement describes.

reason-over-faith.rationale: He told young Germans not to seek Adolf Hitler with their minds but through the strength of their hearts, placing faith above reason.

religion-illusion.rationale: He said he is a deeply religious person, that his belief in God is stronger than most people's, and that he expects God to judge him.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: He treated the Führer as beyond criticism and demanded loyalty.

return-lost-territory.rationale: At Nuremberg he said Danzig and the Polish Corridor were taken from Germany against all rights and that Germany demanded parcels of land.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: He signed the law for the reunion of Austria with Germany in 1938 and praised Sudeten German racial comrades in his 1938 speech.

rule-by-example.rationale: He said that to be a leader is to be an example and that Hitler leads by persuasion rather than command.

sacred-nation.rationale: He said the fallen died for Germany and that Germany will remain united for all eternity, so the nation outlasts its members.

sacred-ruler.rationale: He said Hitler was sent by higher powers and is Germany.

self-interest-moral.rationale: He told party members to think only of the whole National Socialist German people and praised Hitler for doing nothing for himself.

separated-powers.rationale: He said the conscience of a moral leader is a far greater protection against misuse of office than parliamentary supervision or separation of powers.

single-common-good.rationale: He argued that parliamentary majorities represent interest groups and that the leader serves the whole nation rather than balancing competing interests.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: He demanded absolute obedience to the Führer.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: He wrote that the Führer's highest court is his conscience and responsibility to history, not parliament, so the leader is not held to account by constraints on his power.

spiritual-nature.rationale: He wrote of faith, heart, the spirit of the front and providence as central to politics, which treats the spiritual as part of human life.

state-directs-investment.rationale: He praised state-directed construction of highways, canals and buildings as central to the movement's achievements.

strong-leader.rationale: In 1934 he said people in desperate times need an absolute leader whose freedom of action is not restricted by parliamentary bodies.

suppress-opposition.rationale: He announced determined measures against saboteurs and against evil-minded criticism, and said action against critics stops the communists and reactionaries from gaining influence.

territorial-expansion.rationale: As Deputy Führer and Reich minister he signed the Austria law and the decrees taking in the Sudetenland, Danzig and Polish territory (IMT judgment, Austria law).

total-state.rationale: As Deputy Führer he served a state where the party governed everything under a single will.

traditional-family.rationale: He said that preserving the family is essential for racial cleanliness and the future of the German people.

uniformed-youth.rationale: He praised Hitler Youth discipline and uniformed marching.

unions-good.rationale: He said the unions were destroyed as a prerequisite for recovery.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: He held the Führer's will above any other standard and signed laws he accepted responsibility for.

war-builds-character.rationale: He said the front created National Socialism and gave its leaders hardness and camaraderie, while also describing war as a horror he wanted to avoid.

workers-nation.rationale: He presented the working class as part of the German national community and linked the leader to the German working class, against international Marxism.

notes: Hess's record is mostly speeches of 1933-1938 and the decrees and laws he signed. Signed laws are treated as measures only where the tribunal or his office's drafting role is recorded; a signature alone is not a stated view. His 1941 peace terms are known from a British record of his interview with the Duke of Hamilton (cited via the Nuremberg transcript), not from his own words. Later accounts (Spandau, Speer) are secondhand. His claim at Nuremberg of amnesia is recorded by Wikipedia as possibly a ruse. Several speech quotations about Jews and the League of Nations come from Wikipedia and could not be checked against the speech texts, so they are low. Later pass to rules 7 (2026-11-19, claude-sonnet-5-5). Added the Nuremberg-era laws he co-signed (citizenship regulation, Blood Law, Austria law), his final statement and counsel's brief with the Hess-Simon peace terms; his counsel stated he accepted responsibility for every law he signed. Themes searched: leadership, party and state, class and labour, race and citizenship, war and territory, peace terms, trade, law and resistance, religion, economy, environment, technology, family. Answers mixing actions and words were rewritten from the actions alone; one Wikipedia-only answer was nulled. The 1938 Sudeten speech (3258-PS) could not be obtained.
